GTA 6 could already be on your PS5, fully downloaded... and you still can't play it.
So what's stopping it? Picture this.
You pre-order GTA 6. A few days before launch, your PS5 starts downloading it overnight. A huge download.
In the morning, the icon is sitting on your home screen. You press play... and nothing happens.
Here's why. Those files are locked. They're encrypted, scrambled so your console can't open them.
And the key to unlock them isn't part of the preload.
When launch time hits, your PS5 checks in with PlayStation's servers, confirms you own the game, and receives the permission to unlock it.
That's what makes preloading so smart. The giant download happens early, while servers are quiet.
So on launch night, your console only needs a tiny unlock, and maybe a day-one patch, not the whole game while millions of players download at once.
It also helps stop leaks, because nobody can open the files early.
But here's the twist. More and more boxed games come with a download code instead of a disc.
So even if you buy GTA 6 in a store, you could still be downloading it, and waiting for the very same key.
That icon on your home screen? The whole game is already there. It's just waiting for the key.
